instruction: We act for Trilund Pictures Releasing, LLC, an independent film distributor and the licensee under its software license arrangement with Simev Systems, Inc. Trilund Entertainment Group, Inc. and Ostrander Media Holdings, LP are also counterparties in this matter. The client needs a clear picture of where it stands under the license and its related documents so it can decide how to protect its position going forward. Please review everything in the matter folder: the software license agreement (trilund_simev_software_license_agreement.md), Amendment No. 1 (amendment_no_1_software_license_agreement.md), the ReelPath service level schedule (reelpath_service_level_schedule.md), the notice letter dated 2026-10-12 (trilund_notice_letter_2026-10-12.md), and the email thread on the August outage and service credit (email_thread_august_outage_service_credit.md). Then send me a memo that lists each issue you identify. For each one, give the document and section where it appears, explain why it matters for Trilund, and recommend a fix. Where a point is uncertain or depends on facts we don't yet have, say so and tell me what we would need from the client to resolve it.

rubric.text: The response identifies that the Ostrander Media Holdings acquisition of Trilund Entertainment Group, Inc. (Licensee's parent) is a Change of Control under the License Agreement Section 1 definition, and so a deemed assignment under Section 14.2 that requires Simev's prior written consent (which Simev may withhold in its sole discretion). It notes that the October 12, 2026 letter does not request that consent. It locates the issue in the License Agreement (Section 14.2 and/or the Section 1 definition), explains why this matters to Trilund, and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that Amendment No. 1 Section 4 narrows the Section 10.3 liability-cap carve-out so that it covers only breach of Section 7.1, leaving the Section 7.3 obligation to secure Licensee Content subject to the 12-month-fees cap. It identifies that the amendment controls under the Section 16.4 order-of-precedence clause. It locates the issue in Amendment No. 1 (Section 4) and/or License Agreement Section 10.3, explains why this matters to Trilund, and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that under License Agreement Section 12.2, non-renewal notice must be given between October 31 and November 30, 2026 (no more than 120 and no less than 90 days before the February 28, 2027 term end). It concludes that the October 12, 2026 letter is premature and ineffective as non-renewal notice and that the agreement will otherwise renew automatically for a further 36-month term. It locates the issue in License Agreement Section 12.2, explains why this matters to Trilund, and recommends a fix.
The response states that the Initial Term of the License Agreement ends on February 28, 2027 (36 months from March 1, 2024).
The response states that the License Agreement's general liability cap equals the fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim.
The response is a memo that presents each issue separately and, for each issue, gives the document and section, why it matters for Trilund, and a recommended fix.
The response flags at least one point as uncertain or fact-dependent and states what information would be needed from the client to resolve it.
The response claims that Trilund's October 12, 2026 letter is effective notice of non-renewal under Section 12.2.
The response claims that, after Amendment No. 1, breaches of all of Section 7 (including Section 7.3 content security) remain excluded from the liability cap.
